text:
infra-oncall: Alert from fabric-agent at 12:03 UTC — persistent TCP retransmits and ~15-30% packet loss observed in us-west-2b (az-x). Several nodes in gpu-usw2b are failing readiness probes and showing eviction spikes. Investigating.

ben: Can we start diverting inference traffic away from usw2b? latency SLOs are slipping for a small subset of customers. @darren can you coordinate a soft evacuation?

darren: Ack. Starting a soft drain plan. Steps: cordon problem nodes, drain non-critical pods with graceful timeout, keep 2 warm nodes for immediate requests, and update routing preferences. Will not touch scheduled long-running training jobs.

emily: I'll pre-warm capacity in usw2a and usw2c — launching 4 on-demand GPU instances in each as a short-term buffer. Cost impact is acceptable for ~1 hour to stabilize.

carol: Heads-up: embeddings batch jobs will requeue; make sure prefix-KV caches are warmed in target zones so we don't spike token costs with regen. Also watch token-quota throttles for low-tier customers.

deploy-bot: :information_source: Routing policy change applied: prefer_regions=[usw2a,usw2c]; traffic_fraction(usw2b)=0.15 -> 0.02.

ben: Good. @darren, please use staggered drains (30s between nodes) to avoid thundering herd on autoscaler. Keep autoscaler max increased by +6 until we move back.

darren: Commands I'm running now (examples):
```
# cordon and graceful drain
kubectl cordon gpu-node-12 -n inference
kubectl drain gpu-node-12 -n inference --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=600
# update pool scaling profile
redwood-cli pools update gpu-usw2 --max-instances 120
# temporary routing tweak
redwood-router set prefer_regions=usw2a,usw2c --reason "azb packet loss"
```
Drains started on 6 nodes (staggered). Keeping 2 "keep-warm" nodes per rack to serve critical low-latency traffic.

emily: New nodes are up and registered to the pool. Kube readiness probes passing for the new hosts. Starting cache warm: triggering prefix-cache replication to usw2a/usw2c.

carol: Monitoring dashboards: packet loss trend is flattening, but I see an increase in tail latency for rerouted requests — probably cold-cache. Suggest lowering the canary traffic fraction to 5% for legacy customers while caches populate.

infra-oncall: Current plan recap: 1) cordon + staggered soft-drain of affected gpu-usw2b nodes (in progress). 2) scale up on-demand in usw2a/usw2c + pre-warm caches (done). 3) adjust routing to prefer healthy AZs (done). 4) monitor for 30m, if >10% request errors persist, send customer-facing notice. Filing RCA ticket after stabilization.

ben: Estimated drain time ~8-12m per node under graceful 600s; overall should finish ~+45m given stagger and cache warm. Autoscaler bump held.

darren: Drains for first 6 nodes complete. Logs look clean. Leaving nodes cordoned for 20m to ensure no flapping.

deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: Canary routing rollback not needed — current metrics: packet loss in usw2b down to 3%, p95 latency returned to baseline for rerouted traffic.

emily: Observability shows errors dropping. I'll keep the extra on-demand nodes for 30 minutes, then scale down to normal commit.

carol: Opening follow-up action items: (1) run NIC firmware check on affected racks, (2) validate NIC drivers and kernel stats, (3) add more granular SLO alerts for inter-AZ packet loss.

infra-oncall: Thanks team — staying on watch for 40m then moving to postmortem if everything stays green. :thumbsup:

emily: Confirmed stable at 12:49 UTC. Removing temporary capacity in 20m.

ben: Great response. Please capture timeline and commands in the incident ticket.

infra-oncall: Will file ticket and include command snippets + dashboards. Closing thread when RCA created.
